definition.signature: Workers compare blocked/interleaved identical orders and stage timings; switching predicts extra selection/checking independent of layout complexity.
definition.reason: Controlled sequencing tests the archived switching account; tighter controls do not create a mechanism.

definition.signature: Give customers the ordered-layout/short-partition diagram with verified equivalent parts; fewer placement questions distinguishes guidance from physical difficulty.
definition.reason: Same correspondence aid and interpretation-versus-fit discriminator.

definition.signature: Workers stage and independently tally order-specific parts before insertion; reduced selection/checking and omissions, with preparation included.
definition.reason: Trays, mats and bench staging implement checked kits; materials and timing refinements are not new families.

definition.signature: Use ordered silhouettes/identifiers for completeness and corresponding destinations for customer guidance, on a carrier or linked mat/slip; assumes accurate interpretable mapping.
definition.reason: Most predictions combine archived checking and guidance benefits. Improvement beyond either parent alone does not distinguish linkage from their independent combination. Carrier versus reusable mat is a delivery variant.

definition.signature: Independently validate a shared checking/guide map against accepted-order information; detect self-consistent wrong map/kit pairs that internal matching accepts.
definition.reason: Archive assumes dependable parts lists; this tests common-source corruption of that assumption with a distinct seeded-error discriminator.

definition.signature: Cross-swap compatible partitions and slots; failures following part, slot or pairing distinguish causal sources while controlling wear/orientation.
definition.reason: Adds a part-versus-slot-versus-interaction observable beyond the archive's physical-versus-identification distinction.

definition.signature: Use compatibility screening to retain difficult insertions in workshop and transfer easy ones through mapped kits; compare customer retries and total workshop overhead.
definition.reason: Diagnostic result controls task allocation; selective transfer predicts different outcomes from uniformly assembled or unassembled supply.

definition.signature: Insertion resistance deflects a compliant lead-in, exposing a visible misalignment cue before seating; compare witness-only and guide-plus-witness attempts, cues and damage.
definition.reason: Elastic guidance coupled to visible displacement adds an intervention and discriminating comparison absent from the archive.

definition.signature: Earlier partitions obstruct later insertion; short-partition-first versus last changes retries with identical parts, controlling order and loosening.
definition.reason: Procedural obstruction predicts a sequence effect independent of the archive's geometry/identification distinction.

definition.signature: Workers stage and count order-specific parts before insertion; accurate order lists and existing space enable fewer selection errors and shorter selection/checking time.
definition.reason: Trays, mats and staging names retain the checked-kit causal path.

definition.signature: An exact-layout drawing locates the short partition for customers; verified equivalent contents distinguish fewer placement questions from physical insertion failures.
definition.reason: Specific diagrams and interpretation-versus-fit diagnosis already occur in the archive; tighter controls do not create a mechanism.

definition.signature: Workers check occupied partition outlines and carry the corresponding identity into customer placement guidance, with either preassembly or customer insertion; assumes accurate maps and persistent distinguishable correspondence.
definition.reason: Shared correspondence is explicit, but most predicted completeness/placement gains are parent gains. Advantage over equally accurate independent kit checks and instructions remains unresolved; assembly transfer itself is archived.

definition.signature: An order-derived check independent of the shared map detects a self-consistent wrong map/kit pair before release; requires an accurate independent source and genuinely separate checking.
definition.reason: Locally new common-source-error discriminator: internally agreeing aids can pass while the accepted order is wrong. Ordinary kit checking is related but lacks this challenge.

definition.signature: Workers cross-swap compatible partitions and slots on fresh/counterbalanced samples; difficulty tracking part, slot or pair discriminates their contributions.
definition.reason: The archive asks about geometry and interpretation, but does not specify the crossed attribution discriminator.

definition.signature: Compatibility screening assigns difficult insertions to workers and candidate easy insertions to customers through a map carrier; predicts fewer customer retries than uniform transfer, after sorting overhead.
definition.reason: Diagnosis controls task allocation; this predicts a selective-transfer advantage absent from uniform customer assembly.

definition.signature: Changing short-partition insertion order changes access or constraint at later slots; same-part sequence comparisons predict different retry rates without geometry changes.
definition.reason: Procedural obstruction supplies a distinct discriminator beyond the archive geometry/identification question.

definition.signature: Insertion resistance deflects a compliant guide to expose a pre-seating misalignment cue; guide-plus-witness comparisons test cue accuracy, retries and safe repeated removal/loading.
definition.reason: Locally new force-to-deflection feedback mechanism; the archive only investigates insertion problems.

definition.signature: Workers run identical workloads blocked versus interleaved; switching-induced selection/checking delays should decrease independently of layout complexity.
definition.reason: Grouping and stage timing already encode the switching account; matching improves identification rather than novelty.

limits: This compares explicit categories and exact membership sets; it does not adjudicate causal equivalence.
Different reason or signature wording alone is not a disagreement or a novelty finding.
Post-field differences may be encoding differences; adjudication must inspect original text.
No condition labels or mapping files are read.
Unresolved semantic questions must remain uncertain under the frozen selection rule.
